stories.body: Iran's Revolutionary Guard said it struck a tanker in the Strait of Hormuz as President Donald Trump weighed what it described as a major decision on the Iran war. The effective closure of Hormuz, through which roughly a fifth of pre-war global energy supplies passed, is disrupting Gulf exports and pushing Saudi Arabia to move crude by tanker to Oman's Sohar port for ship-to-ship transfers outside the chokepoint. The transfers offer an alternative route but require careful coordination to avoid collisions and spills, while commercial vessels increasingly avoid the strait because of the conflict.
stories.headline: Iran war strains Gulf shipping as the IRGC says it struck a tanker in the Strait of Hormuz

stories.body: The Bank of Japan raised its policy rate from 1% to 1.25%, its highest level since 1995, continuing its departure from decades of ultra-low borrowing costs. The move follows recent rate increases by the US Federal Reserve and European Central Bank as the Iran war's disruption of energy supplies adds to global inflation pressure. Japan, heavily reliant on Middle Eastern energy and coping with a weak yen, has raised rates six times since ending negative rates in 2024; two board members dissented, and analysts expect the bank to remain cautious about further tightening.
stories.headline: Japan raises interest rates to a 31-year high to curb inflation

stories.body: Russia began three days of voting for the State Duma in its first parliamentary election since the full-scale invasion of Ukraine, with President Vladimir Putin's United Russia expected to retain its dominant position. The liberal Yabloko party, the only registered party openly opposing the war, was removed from the party-list ballot by the Supreme Court in August, leaving only parties broadly aligned with the Kremlin on major issues. The vote also includes local and gubernatorial contests, including in occupied parts of Ukraine, as Russians face a slowing economy and increasingly disruptive Ukrainian drone attacks far from the front line.
stories.headline: Russia begins parliamentary voting with meaningful anti-war opposition excluded

stories.body: The Trump administration has notified Congress of a proposed $24.3 billion sale of 48 F-35 stealth fighters to Saudi Arabia, a major shift after years of US reluctance to provide Riyadh with the aircraft. The State Department said the sale would support a major non-NATO ally and would not alter the regional military balance, while Congress has 30 days to review or try to block it. Some lawmakers and defense officials object that Saudi ties with China could expose sensitive technology, and the deal comes as Saudi forces fight Yemen's Iran-backed Houthis.
stories.headline: US approves $24.3 billion sale of 48 F-35 fighter jets to Saudi Arabia

stories.body: At least three people, including a 16-year-old suspected gunman, were killed and eight students were injured in a shooting at Banga National High School in South Cotabato, in the southern Philippines. Officials said two of those killed were 14-year-old students and four of the injured were in critical condition; the suspect reportedly died after shooting himself. Authorities suspended classes across Banga and are investigating reports that may indicate more than one attacker. It is the Philippines' third deadly school shooting since June, prompting renewed calls for adults to secure firearms from minors.
stories.headline: School shooting in the Philippines kills at least three people, including the gunman

stories.body: In-person early voting began six weeks before the November 3 US midterm election, which will decide whether Republicans retain control of both the House and Senate. Major issues include the cost-of-living crisis, the war in Iran and President Donald Trump's aggressive immigration-enforcement campaign. The elections are being closely watched as a test of the administration's political standing and of whether Democrats can regain a congressional chamber.
stories.headline: Early voting begins in US midterms, with control of Congress at stake

stories.body: The White House withdrew President Donald Trump's nomination of a senior Homeland Security aide to lead Immigration and Customs Enforcement after Republican Senator Rand Paul joined Democrats in blocking it. Paul, chair of the Senate Homeland Security Committee, had demanded more information about ICE and Border Patrol shootings that killed two Americans in Minneapolis in January before allowing the nomination to advance. The episode is a setback for the administration's deportation agenda and leaves ICE without a Senate-confirmed director, a position it has not had since 2017.
stories.headline: White House withdraws Trump's nominee to lead ICE after Republican opposition

stories.body: Democratic strategists are advising candidates in competitive races to avoid forceful rhetoric on AI regulation, fearing that industry-backed super PACs could spend heavily against them before the midterms. The caution comes as public concern about advanced AI grows and rival political networks funded by figures linked to OpenAI and Anthropic prepare to influence races. Some Democrats want stronger federal and state safeguards, including export controls, safety reporting and independent audits, but many candidates are balancing those positions against the risk of losing access to technology-sector money.
stories.headline: Democratic candidates tread carefully on AI regulation amid fears of tech super-PAC spending

stories.body: Spanish police and Civil Guard officers began moving hundreds of migrants from encampments on Ceuta's El Trampolín and Benítez beaches to a temporary reception site at the port after the National Court authorized its use. The operation, involving more than 150 officers, was marked by crowding, a rush toward the site and tense confrontations as authorities sought to control the transfer. The camp has space for roughly 1,700 to 1,800 people, far below estimates of more than 3,000 or 4,000 people living at the beaches after the mass arrivals from Morocco in late July.
stories.headline: Spain begins moving migrants from Ceuta's beaches to a temporary port camp after court clearance

stories.body: Spain's government has asked the European Commission for tools to accelerate migrant return procedures during extraordinary crises such as the mass arrivals in Ceuta, while maintaining that people entitled to remain under international law should be protected. Interior Minister Fernando Grande-Marlaska and Migration Minister Elma Saiz made the request in Madrid to the EU migration commissioner, Magnus Brunner. The appeal follows Commission President Ursula von der Leyen's proposal to allow member states greater flexibility in migration rules during exceptional situations, as Spain's opposition presses Brussels to intervene more directly and seek immediate returns to Morocco.
stories.headline: Spain seeks faster EU return procedures for migrants during extraordinary crises such as Ceuta

stories.body: The European Parliament approved a resolution on the mass arrivals in Ceuta that describes the episode as a hybrid threat and calls on Spain to restore normality, while warning Morocco to meet its border-management and migration commitments. Backed by conservative and far-right groups, with socialists, greens and the left opposed, the resolution passed by 339 votes to 225, with 16 abstentions. It stops short of directly accusing Morocco or suspending the EU-Morocco association agreement, but calls for stricter, more transparent rules for EU funding and mechanisms that could permit its suspension.
stories.headline: European Parliament resolution on Ceuta raises the prospect of action against Morocco

stories.body: A 13-year-old unaccompanied Moroccan boy living in a Ceuta reception centre has tested positive for mpox, the autonomous city's first confirmed case since Spain's health alert began. The Carlos III Health Institute confirmed the diagnosis after local health authorities submitted samples. The boy is isolated and receiving treatment, while public-health officials trace contacts and take measures to prevent further transmission; officials say no additional suspected cases have been identified.
stories.headline: A 13-year-old in a Ceuta reception centre tests positive for mpox

stories.body: Barcelona will create a fund to buy commercial premises occupied by historic, emblematic or strategically important neighborhood businesses threatened with closure, Mayor Jaume Collboni announced. The city expects to establish the fund and complete at least one operation before the end of 2026, aiming to protect local commerce from rising rents and acquisition by large chains. Barcelona and the Catalan government are also studying legal changes that would let municipalities exercise pre-emption and withdrawal rights when selected commercial properties are put up for sale.
stories.headline: Barcelona creates a fund to buy emblematic and strategically important shops threatened with closure

stories.body: Mossos d'Esquadra arrested a 21-year-old man suspected of carrying out six copper thefts in 10 days around Barcelona's Estació de França, thefts that severely disrupted rail traffic, including the R2 Sud and southern regional services. Police said the suspect has 14 prior records and was arrested under an outstanding warrant issued by the regional urban-transport investigation unit. Mossos and Adif's private security have reinforced surveillance around the station after the recent thefts, amid data showing that Catalonia accounted for 37.8% of Spain's 409 reported copper thefts in the first half of the year.
stories.headline: Police arrest suspect in six copper thefts at Estació de França that disrupted rail services

stories.body: Workers on Barcelona's Montjuïc cable car have called partial strikes for September 24 and 26, during the La Mercè festivities, and for October 11, citing what they describe as TMB's immobility in negotiations over better social and working conditions. The two-hour stoppages will run from 12:30pm to 2:30pm and from 3:45pm to 5:45pm. The action follows a separate seven-hour bus workers' strike planned for September 22, as TMB bus staff seek a 35-hour workweek, more rest and progress on a collective agreement.
stories.headline: Montjuïc cable-car workers announce partial strikes during La Mercè festivities

stories.body: Six motorcyclists have died in traffic crashes in Barcelona so far in 2026, already exceeding the five deaths recorded during all of 2025 and accounting for nearly half of the city's 13 road fatalities this year. Motorcyclists have been the deadliest-affected road-user group in eight of the past 12 years, while motorcycles make up about 30% of private-vehicle trips in Barcelona. The city's Motorcycle Observatory, created in late 2025, is examining crash-prone locations and aims to halve serious and fatal motorcycle collisions by 2050.
stories.headline: Barcelona sees six motorcyclist deaths in 2026, already exceeding last year's total
